levels.name: Snout tip
levels.region: Rostrum: incisors, canines and the tips of the mandibles
levels.prompt: Can you separate the tooth enamel from the surrounding bone, and see the thin nasal septum between the two nasal passages?

levels.name: Anterior nasal cavity
levels.region: Rostral nasal cavity with the first turbinate scrolls
levels.prompt: How many of the thin, curled turbinate plates can you still trace inside the nasal cavity?

levels.name: Maxilla and teeth
levels.region: Widening nasal cavity, maxillary teeth and mandibular rami
levels.prompt: Can you tell the dense tooth roots from the thinner alveolar bone around them?

levels.name: Posterior nasal cavity
levels.region: Turbinate maze, hard palate and the zygomatic arches
levels.prompt: Follow the thin walls of the turbinate maze. Which settings make them blur together or disappear?

levels.name: Orbital region
levels.region: Narrowing toward the braincase, with the zygomatic arches and palate
levels.prompt: How cleanly can you see the thin bone between the nasal cavity and the braincase?

levels.name: Braincase
levels.region: Cranial vault with the roots of the zygomatic arches
levels.prompt: Look at the inner and outer surfaces of the vault. Are they sharp or smeared?

levels.name: Braincase and bullae
levels.region: Cranial vault and the paired auditory bullae
levels.prompt: Can you resolve the very thin walls of the auditory bullae and the structures inside them?

levels.name: Occipital region
levels.region: Occipital bone with the bullae and petrous region
levels.prompt: This is the most complex, thin-walled region. Which settings keep its fine detail intact?

scans.note: A stronger beam-hardening correction than the baseline's 0.1. Faint bright streaks start to appear around the dense mandibles and zygomatic arches.
A very strong beam-hardening correction. It overcorrects: bright streaks fan out from the dense mandibles and zygomatic arches, and the bone looks less uniform.
Run as an over-exposure test (the scan was named 'oversaturated'): the detector signal saturates and broad streaks cross the whole slice.

Run as an over-exposure test (the scan was named 'oversaturated'): the detector signal saturates and broad streaks cross the whole slice. At 200 kV, switching the beam-hardening correction between 0 and 0.1 changes this image very little.
Run as an under-exposure test (the scan was named 'undersaturated'): low X-ray energy means little signal gets through thick bone.
